page: Amazon Web Services r8id.96xlarge is a high-density, memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System. It is equipped with dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors featuring 192 physical cores and 384 vCPUs running at up to 3.9 GHz. The system delivers 3072 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 memory, maintaining an 8 GB memory-to-vCPU allocation. Advanced acceleration extensions, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), are integrated alongside a 480 MB L3 cache.

Storage and connectivity are engineered for enterprise scale, integrating 22800 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside 100 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks indicate exceptional throughput under heavy concurrent loads. The instance achieved top-tier rankings in multi-core stress testing (414,984.2 on stress-ng) and database execution (33,652.72 on PassMark database operations). High-speed caching is demonstrated by 451.6 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and uncached read memory bandwidth exceeding 1.1 TB/s.

While general compute and compression tasks scale predictably, the absence of discrete GPUs limits autonomous text generation rates in large language models. The platform instead optimizes cost efficiency around immense in-memory capacity and local NVMe density, removing external storage latency. The r8id.96xlarge is suitable for enterprise in-memory databases like SAP HANA and Redis, extensive real-time analytical processing, relational database scaling, and distributed build environments.
